newsitem.title: POLAND: FORECAST - Polish year-end inflation at 16.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Polish year-end inflation at 16.7 pct.

text.p: Polish bankers expect year-on-year inflation in December 1997 to ease to 16.7 percent from 18.5 percent in December 1996, a poll by the private Pentor institute showed.
Bank managers polled by Pentor last month expected inflation to end the year at 16.8 percent against the government's forecast, which sees inflation ending this year at 13 percent.
The 207 bankers polled in February also expected the dollar to end the year at 3.24 zlotys, up from its current market stance at 3.01 zlotys and 3.06 in the last month's forecast.

They also predicted a slight fall in interest rates this year, with lombard rate falling 1.3 point to 23.7 percent. Credit for enterprises is expected to fall 1.1 point to 22.5 percent and the three-month deposit rate to 16.4 percent.
The Pentor survey is commissioned monthly by the Polish Banking Association (ZBP).
